clue.text: Don acting in plays calls for liquid refreshment

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a new arrangement, so they are anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A university don performing on stage asks for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' turns DON ACTING IN into a new eleven-letter arrangement; 'calls for' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This classic mixed drink of spirit and quinine water is a liquid refreshment.

clue.text: Terrible danger complaint of police officer

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word danger is mangled into a new order

parts.note: ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, a medical complaint

explanation.surface: A dreadful threat, the grumble of a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' signals the anagram; ME, the medical condition myalgic encephalomyelitis, is a stock crossword 'complaint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French armed policeman.

clue.text: Dope on Arctic trip

indicators.note: a trip upsets things, and the drug sense of trip hints at disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking drugs while on a polar expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a drug, especially one that dulls the senses.

clue.text: Required up river between poles?

definitions.note: the definition is a past participle; the answer is the verb as in 'it needs doing'

indicators.note: between places one piece inside the two letters of the other

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales

explanation.surface: A question about what is needed travelling upriver between polar regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that must be had is wanted as a necessity.

clue.text: Significant uttering

definitions.meaning: striking or revealing, as a revealing remark
saying or relating, as in recounting a story

explanation.definitionFit: A revealing detail is striking, and recounting something is speaking it.

clue.text: Vengeance is seen with bit of malice, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way
a bit of a word is its first letter here

explanation.surface: Revenge is witnessed with a touch of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IS SEEN plus M, the first letter of 'malice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Greek goddess of retribution, it means downfall or retribution.

clue.text: One of a pair for the Chinese?

definitions.text: One of a pair for the Chinese?

parts.words: One of a pair for the Chinese?
parts.note: suggests a matching item for a person, but means one of two eating sticks, and 'the Chinese' is also a takeaway meal

explanation.definitionFit: Eating utensils used in twos in East Asian cuisine.

clue.text: String not right to get fish

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is to be left out of the string

parts.note: a cord is a string

explanation.surface: A piece of string missing its right-hand part still catches a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Place one advert in The Accountant

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the abbreviation for accountant

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Instructions to put an advertisement in the accountancy journal.
explanation.walkthrough: CA stands for chartered accountant; 'Place' is a noun here, a country on the map, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a place on the map.

clue.text: Tailless dog goes around old city all the while

indicators.note: goes around has one piece encircle the other
tailless says the last letter of the dog is dropped

parts.note: a dingo is an Australian wild dog
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A bobtailed hound circles an ancient settlement throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout a period, as in 'throughout the meal'.

clue.text: Tend to dash back to the London area

indicators.note: back tells us the word for dash is read from right to left

parts.note: to dash is to run
SE is the London postal area, also the south-east of England

explanation.surface: Instructions to look after someone by rushing back to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient is to care for them as a hospital carer does.

clue.text: One to ridicule room panel being rebuilt

indicators.note: a rebuilt structure has its parts put together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone renovating a room has a wall panel reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rebuilt' rearranges ROOM and PANEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist who mocks people in print or verse is one who ridicules.

clue.text: Sound science

parts.note: reads as reliable, well-founded research, but means the branch of physics that studies how noise travels

explanation.definitionFit: The study of how noise is produced and transmitted is the physics of hearing.

clue.text: Chair lift

parts.note: reads as a ski-slope cable car, but describes an enclosed seat carried on poles by bearers

explanation.definitionFit: An old covered seat carried by two porters gave its passenger a lift in a chair.

clue.text: But it could have more than seven letters!

definitions.text: But it could have more than seven letters!

parts.words: But it could have more than seven letters!
parts.note: seems to remark on the length of a word, but describes a postman's sack holding many items of post

explanation.walkthrough: The answer itself has seven letters, so the clue teases that it holds more 'letters' in the postal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal sack carries far more pieces of correspondence than seven.

clue.text: Play a flop? I cast afresh using extravagant language

parts.note: a play that flops is said to bomb, and a failure is a bomb

indicators.note: afresh says the letters are cast again in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre producer whose show failed decides to recast it in grandiloquent terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' signals the anagram; a theatrical flop is said to bomb, and the surface's recast play hides that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous and inflated speech is high-flown.

clue.text: Peg's backing a certainty

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the word for pegs from right to left

parts.note: pegs, read as a plural with the apostrophe ignored, are pins

explanation.surface: Peg is supporting a dead cert, as at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang this word means a sure thing or an easy bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a cinch or a sure thing.

clue.text: Protection against rust mainly below the surface

indicators.note: mainly tells us most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: underseal is a coating applied to the underside of a car to prevent corrosion

explanation.surface: Anti-corrosion treatment largely applied beneath the visible level.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERSEAL is the British name for the anti-rust coating under a car; 'mainly' drops its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath the waves is submarine.

clue.text: Lively

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as the single word 'Lively' (8): no wordplay or second definition survives in the OCR and no source found to restore it.

clue.text: Some youngsters meet the pirate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of children are introduced to a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook's bosun in Peter Pan is a well-known fictional buccaneer.

clue.text: Back the last one in National 'unt Race?

parts.note: the end is the last part
a runner in the Grand National is a horse; with the dropped H of 'unt it becomes 'orse

explanation.surface: Support the final runner in a Grand National hunt race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British steeplechase; the apostrophe in 'unt signals that the H is dropped from horse too.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate is to support them publicly.

clue.text: Extra long garment could be adopted

definitions.meaning: a dress too long can be shortened by raising its hem
accepted, as a hobby or an offer is accepted

explanation.surface: A dress that is too long might be altered, or taken on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortening by raising the hem, and accepting an offer, are both expressed by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Let us wander around the ship to get scraps

indicators.note: around has the rearranged letters surround the other piece
wander says the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: An invitation to stroll the deck to collect fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wander' rearranges LET US to TULES, which goes 'around' SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are fights or scuffles.

clue.text: Sort to show a film

definitions.meaning: sift or separate, as when candidates are vetted
project a movie in a cinema

explanation.definitionFit: Vetting by sifting, and projecting a movie, are both meanings.

clue.text: Burning forest trees initially

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland of Shakespeare's As You Like It

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Woodland with its trees ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and fervent feelings are fiery.

clue.text: Around Central America to gather heart of birch

indicators.note: to gather is to collect inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America

indicators.note: the heart of a word is everything but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trip through Central America to collect birch wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word placed before a date means approximately.

clue.text: Aid sapper to camouflage, cease to be visible

indicators.note: camouflage disguises the look of something, so these letters are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: Helping a military engineer hide himself from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to camouflage' rearranges AID and SAPPER; a sapper is a military engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to stop being seen.

clue.text: Work on the pipes? Precisely

definitions.meaning: do a ... job on water pipes
exactly, as in 'right in the middle'

explanation.definitionFit: Fitting water pipes, and exactly, as in 'bang in the centre'.

clue.text: Opt for an examination of the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose or opt for
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Choosing to sit a test about the electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to elections and the people who cast ballots.

clue.text: At college a certain group is confused

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a set is a particular group

explanation.surface: A clique at university is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown into disorder or distressed is being in a muddle.

clue.text: The butterfly catcher is clear of charges

definitions.meaning: a mesh on a pole used by lepidopterists
after deductions, as with pay or profit after tax

explanation.definitionFit: A mesh used to trap insects, and an amount remaining after deductions.

clue.text: See bod reach out for a selection at table

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written; bod is British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Watch a fellow stretch his arm out to pick something at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter offering assorted cheeses is served as a choice at the end of dinner.
